recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If malformed extension JSON templates reappear in generated output, investigate HL7/kindling or the publisher dependency rather than editing FHIR narrative/template files in this checkout.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core correction reporting malformed generated text in extension-definition JSON templates: an empty Extension.extension array showed `sliced by value:url in the specified orderOpen` with confusing brackets. Jira comments clarified that this applied to all extension pages, not just the example 11179/DataElement extension.
initial_application: The Jira comment records `svn revision 12694`. In git, that is be4ab1e77319083d7653c1ba5e02c1c5ee3deff9 (`#13473 - clean up json slicing text`), which changed the old in-repository JsonSpecGenerator to close empty sliced arrays correctly and avoid concatenating the slicing rule display directly onto `order`.
additional_context: The old generator file was deleted in 2021 when publishing moved to the Kindling dependency. The current checkout declares `org.hl7.fhir:kindling` in build.gradle.kts and `kindlingVersion=1.25.5-SNAPSHOT` in gradle.properties. Current HL7/kindling JsonSpecGenerator retains the fixed empty-slice and slicing-description logic. The current extension page template only injects `<%json%>`, and searches of current core source and the read-only extension-pack checkout found no active occurrence of the malformed text. Zulip confirms the original publisher-bug report; Confluence and later searches found no conflicting decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. The current FHIR checkout has no necessary source edit because the historical fix is already applied in the current publisher path and the active template source is not wrong.
